name: Petrarchan desire and the sonnet mistress
description: The conventions of Petrarchan love — the idealized and unattainable mistress, the lover's service and frustration, the icy fire of desire — and their English transformation into wit, parody, and self-examination.

name: Ambition and the overreacher
description: The protagonist who aspires beyond human limits — Tamburlaine's conquest, Faustus's knowledge, Macbeth's crown — and the moral and cosmic consequences of boundless will.

name: Revenge and justice
description: The imperative of vengeance, the tension between private revenge and public justice, and the moral and theological problems posed by the revenger's act.

name: Appearance, dissembling, and self-fashioning
description: The gap between seeming and being: disguise, hypocrisy, the fashioning of the self for court or city, and the theatricality of social life.

name: Order and degree: the body politic
description: The hierarchical conception of the commonwealth as a body, the dangers of disorder and rebellion, and the duties of rule and obedience.

name: Time, death, and immortality through verse
description: The ravages of time on beauty and love, and the poet's claim to confer immortality through the monument of verse.

name: The public theatre and the players' world
description: The theatre's own world — players, playwrights, audiences, and the business of the playhouse — reflected back in plays about acting and performance.

name: Colonial enterprise and the New World
description: English exploration, conquest, and settlement in America and the East; the discovery literature of Hakluyt, Ralegh, and Purchas; and the imaginative consequences for Utopia, The Tempest, and the masque.

name: Melancholy and self-analysis
description: The Elizabethan and Jacobean fashion for melancholy, the anatomy of the self, and the introspective modes of Hamlet, Donne, and Burton.

name: Divine love and holy desire
description: The love of God and the soul's desire for union with the divine, treated with the language of human love in the religious lyric and the devotional prose.

name: Patronage and the literary marketplace
description: The dependence of authors on noble patronage and on the new commercial market of the playhouse and the printing house, and the literary politics of dedication, complaint, and professional authorship.

name: Women, chastity, and constancy
description: The conduct and reputation of women, the double standard of chastity, and the assertion of female virtue and voice by both male and female authors.
